status.nb: 10 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 25 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Caracas, Valencia og Maracaibo.

summary.en: The Venezuelan army bombed an ELN guerrilla camp in Apure, killing at least 19 rebels, and a U.S. drone strike hit an ELN drug depot nearby, causing at least 20 deaths. Rubio says the United States is in talks to establish a military presence in Venezuela and has floated a one-day operation to capture Maduro. The U.S. military is coordinating with Venezuela to launch drone strikes on cartels, and Trump defended the Hegseth amid an impeachment threat while citing successful operations in Iran and Venezuela. 2 battle-related deaths in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Den venezuelanske hæren bombet en ELN-gerilja-leir i Apure, og drepte minst 19 opprørere, og et amerikansk droneram angrep et ELN-drogdepot i nærheten, og forårsaket minst 20 dødsfall. Rubio sier at USA er i samtaler om å etablere en militær tilstedeværelse i Venezuela og har foreslått en ett-dags operasjon for å fange Maduro. Det amerikanske militæret koordinerer med Venezuela for å gjennomføre droneram mot karteller, og Trump forsvaret Hegseth midt i en riksrettstrussel mens han henviste til vellykkede operasjoner i Iran og Venezuela. 2 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro as well as Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
